response.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT t.equipstatus, AVG(g.pulsepersec) AS avg_p FROM signals g JOIN telescopes t ON g.telescref = t.telescregistry WHERE g.pulsepersec IS NOT NULL GROUP BY t.equipstatus), m1 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_p) AS mean1 FROM s), k AS (SELECT s.equipstatus, s.avg_p, s.avg_p - m1.mean1 AS ex1, m1.mean1 FROM s CROSS JOIN m1 WHERE s.avg_p > m1.mean1), m2 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_p) AS mean2 FROM k) SELECT AVG(k.avg_p) AS avg_pulse_rate_average, AVG(k.ex1) AS avg_excess_over_first_mean, AVG(k.avg_p - m2.mean2) AS avg_excess_over_second_mean FROM k CROSS JOIN m2 WHERE k.avg_p > m2.mean2

assumptions.assumption: Statuses with NULL equipstatus form their own group (or are excluded by being NULL in the group); a NULL-status group is treated like any other group by GROUP BY and would count in the first mean.
The 'mean of status averages' is an unweighted mean of per-status averages, not a signal-weighted mean.
If no status survives the second filter (e.g., only one status kept), the result is a row of NULLs, since the strict 'above' comparison excludes it.
